sources: rules/ARCHITECTURE.md in this case (application layer: sibling packages form an acyclic graph; a shared type lives in a module both sides import)
Acyclic Dependencies Principle (concept: no cycles among sibling packages; break a cycle by moving the shared type to a module both sides import)

defects.description: Line 5 is from orders.service import OrderStatus. Together with code/orders/service.py line 7 (from refunds.repo import RefundRepo), the modules orders.service and refunds.repo import each other, forming a cycle inside the application layer. The rule requires the application-layer packages to form an acyclic graph and requires a shared type to live in a module both sides import. OrderStatus is owned by orders.service and read by refunds.repo, so the cycle is created by this change. Import-time failure is possible depending on the entry point, and the two packages cannot be changed or tested independently.
defects.evidence: Static check, grep -n over code/: code/orders/service.py:7 'from refunds.repo import RefundRepo'; code/refunds/repo.py:5 'from orders.service import OrderStatus'. Both edges are added lines in change.diff (hunks at orders/service.py and refunds/repo.py). Runtime import order not executed.

decoys.why_not_a_defect: One-way import from refunds.service to refunds.repo. Nothing in refunds.repo or any sibling imports refunds.service, so no cycle is formed. The edge follows the rule's acyclic graph. Evidence: grep -n over code/ shows refunds/service.py:5 'from refunds.repo import RefundRepo, RefundRow' and no import of refunds.service anywhere under code/.
